newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf wargames friendly, show Islam's might -Iran.
newsitem.headline: Gulf wargames friendly, show Islam's might -Iran.

text.p: Iran's largest wargames convey a message of peace and friendship to Gulf states while displaying the might of Islam, a senior Iranian commander said as Iran paraded its naval power in the strategic waterway on Wednesday.

State-run Tehran radio said 180 Revolutionary Guards vessels -- missile-launching frigates, light craft and speedboats -- manoeuvred under the gaze of supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei at the strategic port of Bandar Abbas overlooking the Strait of Hormuz.
The parade, close to shipping lanes at the mouth of the vital oil-export waterway, demonstrated the forces' firm resolve "to defend the precious heritage of our martyrs", it said.
Tests firings of surface-to-air, shore-to-sea and surface-to-surface missiles were due to take place during the three-day wargames.

Not far across the horizon warships of the U.S. Fifth Fleet monitored the Iranian manoeuvres. The United States keeps warships in the Gulf as part of President Bill Clinton's dual containment policy aimed at isolating Iran and Iraq.
Khamenei, successor to the late founder of the Islamic republic Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, is commander-in-chief of Iran's 500,000-strong armed forces.
Some 200,000 elite members of the guards -- defenders of the 1979 revolution which toppled the monarchy -- and Basij militia volunteers are taking part in the amphibious wargames.
The exercises -- code-named "Tariq ol-Qods" (Road to Jerusalem) -- cover the whole of the Gulf and spread through four of Iran's provinces from the entrance to the Gulf to the border with Iraq.

Mohammad Baqer Zolqadr, head of the Revolutionary Guards joint command headquarters, said in Bandar Abbas that the wargames aimed to upgrade defensive power while conveying a message of peace and friendship to regional countries, and to display the might of Islam, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said.
Iran's oil-rich Gulf Arab neighbours have been alarmed by an Iranian military buildup despite Tehran's assurances that it was defensive.
IRNA also quoted Zolqadr as saying land and sea operations had been designed to test Iran's defence potential to counter simultaneous hypothetical threats in the west and south.

Frigates, fast patrol boats, aircraft and helicopters took part in the parade. The guards launched 10 patrol boats equipped with Iranian-built Tondar (Thunder) missile launchers guards on Tuesday evening at the start of the wargames. Tehran radio said the Tondar missiles had a range of 120 km (75 miles).

The guards deputy commander, Brigadier-General Rahim Safavi, said the wargames were defensive in nature. They would include major amphibious exercises in the Strait of Hormuz, through which more than 15 million barrels of oil -- half the world's oil exports -- pass each day.
IRNA said Khamenei inspected the Qadr missile-launching vessel at Iran's main naval base in Bandar Abbas where he was briefed on its military and defence capabilities and features.
He also inspected an exhibition of the Revolutionary Guard naval forces displaying achievements in the areas of research and self-sufficiency including missile projects.
